verses.text: Jacob looked up, and there was Esau coming with his four hundred men. So he divided the children among Leah, Rachel and the two slave women.
He put the slave women and their children in front, Leah and her children next, and Rachel and Joseph at the back.
He himself went on ahead of them, and he bowed down to the ground seven times as he came near his brother.
But Esau ran to meet Jacob and hugged him. He threw his arms around his neck and kissed him, and they wept.
Then Esau looked up and saw the women and children. "Who are these with you?" he asked. Jacob answered, "They are the children God has kindly given your servant."
Then the slave women and their children came near and bowed down.
Next, Leah and her children came and bowed down. Last of all came Joseph and Rachel, and they too bowed down.
Esau asked, "What do you mean by all these herds I met?" "They are to win your favour, my master," Jacob said.
But Esau said, "I already have plenty, my brother. Keep what you have for yourself."
"No, please," said Jacob. "If you are pleased with me, accept this gift from me. To see your face is like seeing the face of God, now that you have welcomed me so kindly.
Please accept the gift that was brought to you, because God has been kind to me, and I have everything I need." Because Jacob kept on asking him, Esau accepted it.
Then Esau said, "Let's be on our way. I will go with you."

But Jacob said to him, "My master knows that the children are weak, and that I have to take care of the sheep and cattle that are feeding their young. If they are driven hard for even one day, all the animals will die.
So let my master go on ahead of his servant, while I move along slowly at the pace of the flocks and herds in front of me and at the pace of the children, until I come to my master in Seir."
Esau said, "Then let me leave some of my men with you." "Why do that?" Jacob asked. "It is enough that my master is pleased with me."
So that day Esau started back on his way to Seir.
But Jacob went to Succoth. There he built a house for himself and made shelters for his livestock. That is why the place is called Succoth, which means "shelters".
After Jacob came from Paddan Aram, he arrived safely at the city of Shechem in Canaan and set up camp near the city.
For a hundred pieces of silver, he bought the piece of land where he had put up his tent. He bought it from the sons of Hamor, the father of Shechem.
There he set up an altar and called it El Elohe Israel, which means "God, the God of Israel".
